world.bio: Filipina nanny for a family in Jumeirah for five years. I look after two children, aged six and nine, from seven in the morning to seven at night, six days a week. I send most of my pay home to my parents in Cebu, and I study cabin-crew interview videos at night in my room. Friday is my day off. I'm learning to swim at a community pool on Fridays, and my sister's wedding is in December in Cebu. I'm saving for a small plot of land back home.
skills_assets: Five years of experience as a live-in nanny in Jumeirah, caring for two children
English fluency (Filipino-English), basic Arabic phrases from the family and the market
Good with children: homework help, meal prep, first aid, swimming supervision
A habit of studying interview videos at night: I know the standard cabin-crew questions by heart
A phone full of saved videos, notes and a spreadsheet of airline requirements
A friend network of Filipino domestic workers in Dubai, who meet in Karama on Fridays

projects.name: Cabin crew application
projects.text: I want to apply for cabin crew before I turn 30 next year. I've watched hundreds of videos. Open days are on weekdays, and I only get Fridays off. Academies in Dubai charge around 3,000 dirhams for a full course, and I can't afford it; my savings are for the land. I've been practising in front of my phone, saying 'Why do you want to be cabin crew?' over and over, working on my smile, my grooming, and my reach test (I'm 160cm and need to touch a mark at 212cm).

projects.name: Swimming lessons
projects.text: Friday mornings at a community pool in Al Barsha. My instructor is patient. I'm learning freestyle but I still panic when my feet leave the floor. The airlines require swimming ability, which is part of why I started.

notes.text: Boss's mother visited and said I was 'part of the family'. Then she asked me to polish the silver. Part of the family polishes silver? I smiled and polished it.

Studied a video last night: 'Top 10 cabin crew interview questions'. 'Tell us about a time you handled a difficult passenger.' I thought about the nine-year-old at 6pm when she refuses to eat. That's my story. I practised saying it in a way that sounded professional.
Sister's wedding is in December. I need to send 4,000 pesos for the dress. I have 3,200 dirhams saved for the land, but I'm not touching it. I will send my December bonus.
Friday at the pool. Swam two lengths without stopping, almost. Coach said, 'Maricel, you did it.' I almost cried in the water. First time I felt my body was mine.
Madam asked if I'd be willing to move with them to Abu Dhabi next year. I said I'll think about it. I know it's a compliment, but it also feels like a door closing. I told no one.

A friend from Karama showed me a flyer for a cabin crew academy: 3,000 AED, 8 weeks, weekday evenings only. I don't have weekday evenings. I'm with the kids until seven, then dinner, then bath. She said maybe ask Madam for Wednesday evenings off. I haven't dared.

Mock interview with my friend Joy. She played the interviewer. 'Why should we hire you?' I said 'Because I have five years of caring for people and I stay calm in emergencies'. Joy said, 'That sounds like a nanny CV.' I laughed. It is.
Called my mum. She said Papa's knees are worse. I said I'll send more. She said don't worry, take care of yourself. I said I always do. We both knew it wasn't true.
Nine-year-old said, 'Maricel, are you going to leave us?' I said not yet. She said, 'Good, because I'd cry.' I told her I'd cry too. Then she asked me to help with her maths homework.

messages.text:
Joy: Fri evening, Karama? We can practise.
Maricel: Yes, I'll bring the questions.
Joy: Wear your hair up like the crew.
Maricel: OK!

Mum: Did you get the money for the dress?
Maricel: Sending next week.
Mum: Don't skip meals.
Maricel: I don't.

Madam: Can you stay until 8 on Thursday? We have guests.
Maricel: Of course.
Madam: Thank you, you are wonderful.

Faisal: Next Friday, we try floating on the back.
Maricel: OK, I'm scared.
Faisal: You'll be fine.
